title: Duke Frederik of Schleswig-Holstein and Lübeck, negotiation papers 1523 with name signs (Rigsarkivet, Sønderjyske Fyrstearkiver, Hertug Frederik (1.), Sager vedrørende udlandet, item 8)

documents.route: Duke Frederik (Gottorp) to the council of Lübeck; chancery draft/copy

plaintext.source: Hanserecesse III/8 (Schäfer and Techen 1910) n. 292, pp. 324-326: the letter printed with every sign resolved from the key strip (Gemeinsch. Arch. cap. XIII, 38), witness K1 = 'XIII, 47 c, Konzept'; the key reproduced on the plate facing p. 312

transcription.notes: First-pass transcription of the page (30 lines, 51 sign tokens, 15 sign types) made before the edition was found; its sign labels agree with the edition's Ch. numbers. The rest of item 8 (images 95-129) was not transcribed.

system.summary: Clear Low German with single graphic signs for names: 72 numbered signs on the key strip (Sundays of Lent to Pentecost, weekdays, persons, places, rutere/knechte/krygesvolck, one null 'nichts bedudende'), plus a letter alphabet that the editors say was not used.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = signs on the key strip. Per the edition, the code is used in Lübeck-Frederik letters from n. 279 (1 Feb 1523) to n. 354. The circle-bar sign (Ch. 28, hertog Frederich) also stands where the clear draft K2 has 'wy'.

prior_solution.where: Hanserecesse III/8 (1910), n. 279 note 1 and plate facing p. 312 (key), n. 292 pp. 324-326 (this letter, signs resolved); also nn. 278, 279, 293, 299, 309, 312

conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue task; no other input.

solution.what: Web search for Frederik/Lübeck 1523 cipher; 7 Hanserecesse III-series scans on archive.org checked by text: none is Bd. 8.
Whole series (epid 14908271, ids from 41301821) downloaded; item slips located by contact sheets; item 8 = images 94-129 (slip at 93, item 9 slip at 130).
Image 94 viewed: clear Low German with single signs in place of names; 15 sign types on the page; identified as a name-sign code, not a letter cipher.
Image 94 transcribed line by line with sign labels (30 lines, 50 sign tokens).

From context: the two signs counted in 'den bedungeden tall der GG vnd IIII' are troops (ships or soldiers); the rectangle is King Christian ('deme SQ aftobrekende'); QX a prince with territory on the troops' route.

Hanserecesse III/8 found as a Hansischer Geschichtsverein PDF; n. 292 is this letter (witness K1 = XIII 47c, 'chiffrirt'), printed with every sign resolved; the key strip (Gemeinsch. Arch. XIII, 38, endorsed by Wolf von Utenhof) is reproduced on the plate facing p. 312. GG = rutere (Ch. 64), IIII = knechte (65), SQ = koningk (27), QX = bisschop van Bremen (33), CB = hertog Frederich (28), CX = Lübeck (41).

Own transcription of image 94 compared with the printed text and its Ch. footnotes: every sign label falls on one Ch. number, and the four small signs of line 21 are Ch. 58, 59, 56, 60 (Sehelandt, Fune, Copenhagen, Schonen) as printed.
Key plate transcribed to key.tsv (72 values with sign descriptions).

Disagreements with the print checked on the scan: l.16 is the Lübeck sign (first pass had the Frederik sign; corrected); l.10 shows the Frederik sign where the edition gives Ch. 41 Lübeck for K1 (sense needs Lübeck; recorded, not changed).

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): image 94 collated sign by sign with the apparatus of Hanserecesse III/8 n. 292 (verify_dudout_20261114.py): the edition gives 51 signs for K1 (image 94), the transcription has 51 labels; 50/51 agree, the one difference being the l. 10 sign already recorded; key.tsv values found in decryption_094.txt 51/51. Of the ten words given 'as printed', l. 29 <durchtheent> is not the printed text (L reads durchthendes; durchtheent is in a passage struck out in the drafts, note l*); decryption_094.txt corrected to <durchthendes>. v10 read_share 1.0 unchanged.

Project check of PR #572 (Brice Dudout): his collation script re-run (51 K1 signs in the edition's apparatus, 51 labels in transcription_094.txt, 50 agree, the l. 10 sign being the known difference; 51 of 51 key values stand in the decryption). The count '50 sign tokens' of the transcription step is 51; the ciphertext note corrected. l. 29 checked in Hanserecesse III/8 n. 292 (PDF p. 345): the printed text has 'krygesvolk durchthendes', note a* gives 'knechte adir rutere' for K1; his correction of <durchtheent> to <durchthendes> stands. No key correction.

texts.label: Image 94: Frederik to Lübeck, Gottorp, 15 Feb 1523 (Hanserecesse III/8 n. 292, witness K1)
texts.summary: Frederik reports that he has put off the meeting with the Jutland nobles at Haderslev to Reminiscere because his troops are not assembled and King Christian is strong; he asks Lübeck to have the agreed horsemen and foot soldiers ready by Invocavit, to press its troops and the Swedes against Zealand, Funen, Copenhagen and Scania, and reports 4000 soldiers gathering in Oldenburg for the king, whose passage he has asked the Bishop of Bremen to block.
texts.note: Signs resolved with the 1910 key plate; nine words left uncertain in the first-pass transcription are given as printed in n. 292 (marked < > in the decryption). Image 95 (the rest of the letter) not transcribed; the whole letter is printed in Hanserecesse III/8 pp. 324-326.

reading_review.note: Clear Low German with names resolved; every sentence reads. The page is the first half of the letter.
